questions.q: Why does this lesson say a presentation structured as "here's the data model, here's the Apex, here's the LWC" is the wrong approach for this audience?
options: Because it takes too long to prepare
Because it talks to Priya's architecture interest for the whole time and loses Renata's business interest and Dmitri's operational interest
Because Apex cannot be presented without live code
Because data models should never be shown in a presentation
questions.explain: Renata, Priya, and Dmitri have different interests in the room; a purely technical walkthrough only serves Priya and loses the other two audiences.

questions.q: In the four-section presentation structure, what does the "Architecture highlights" section cover?
options: Every file in the Salesforce DX project, in order
A read-through of the entire data dictionary
The full quiz bank from every lesson
Two or three ADRs chosen for their genuine trade-offs, not a tour of every file
questions.explain: The lesson specifies selecting two or three ADRs with genuine trade-offs for Priya's section, rather than exhaustively touring every file.

questions.q: Where does the answer to "Why Queueable and not Platform Events for the warranty submission?" come from, per this lesson?
options: It has to be improvised live during the presentation
It is not actually answerable and should be deflected
ADR-004 from Lesson 21, which already documents that Platform Events were considered and rejected as unnecessary complexity
The quiz from Lesson 11
questions.explain: ADR-004 already documents this exact alternative and the reason it was rejected, so the presentation doesn't require improvising a justification on the spot.

questions.q: What is the "what's next" section of the presentation framed as, per this lesson, rather than as an apology?
options: The known technical debt from Lesson 22's retrospective, framed as a deliberate roadmap
A list of bugs that were never fixed
A request for a budget increase
A full re-explanation of the Definition of Done
questions.explain: The lesson frames the known technical debt as a deliberate roadmap item, not something to apologize for -- consistent with Lesson 22's point that documented debt is a sign of honest engineering, not failure.

questions.q: How does this lesson distinguish this capstone's presentation from the Architecture Review Board defense in the next course?
options: They require entirely different, unrelated skills
This capstone's presentation has a Board of unfamiliar architects too
The next course's defense does not involve architecture decisions at all
The underlying skill (defending a decision with evidence) is the same, but the audience, stakes, and scale go up considerably in the next course's enterprise-scale Architecture Review Board defense
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly says the skill (evidence-based defense) carries forward, but the audience (architects unfamiliar with the project), stakes, and scale (full enterprise transformation) increase in the next course.
